messages.subject: Model selection
parts:
Dear Distance sampling,

Today i was modeling my data dan came upon these errors. 

Half-normal key with cosine adjustments -> Warning in mrds::check.mono(model, n.pts = 20) : Detection function is not strictly monotonic!

Hazard-rate key with polynomial adjustments -> In ds(data = TD6SWP, key = "hr", adjustment = "poly", truncation = 45.5, : 
Estimated hazard-rate scale parameter close to 0 (on log scale). Possible problem in data (e.g., spike near zero distance). 

I can't seem to figure out why the models give these error codes. The strange part is also that these models with warnings have the lowes AIC scores and seem to fit the dataset the best when plotting them and visually comparing them with the half-normal key with hermite adjustments and uniform key with cosine adjustments. 

Can i still utilize the models with the warning messages to determine population size and denstiy or should i discard the model and utilize one with a higher AIC and slight lesser fit to the dataset?

Thank you in advance. 

With kind regards, 

Casolyn

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Model selection
parts:
Casolyn

The messages are warnings, not errors. Warnings are issued when the software does things (fitting models) about which it is uncomfortable. Granted software does not have feelings, but if it did, it would sometimes be "uncomfortable".

In the first instance (not strictly monotonic) the software has fitted a detection function where detection probability increases as a function of distance over some range of distances. This is something detection functions don't usually do. The software is alerting you to this, suggesting you make the determination regarding the appropriateness of a detection function with this shape.

The second warning (hazard rate scale parameter very small) is issued when the software fits a detection function that falls off very rapidly with distance. As the message notes, this may be caused by data with a spike (many detections) at very small distances. You showed a histogram of detection distances that looked like this in your email on Wednesday. Again, the software is asking you to make a determination as to whether a detection function of this shape is biologically plausible.

Use AIC as a guide in model selection, it is not the only factor to be used in model selection.
